newsitem.title: FRANCE: French priests want "Larry Flynt" poster banned.
newsitem.headline: French priests want "Larry Flynt" poster banned.

text.p: Roman Catholic priests have asked a Paris court to ban a poster advertising "The People vs Larry Flynt", a film by Milos Forman on pornography and press freedom, their lawyer said on Monday.
On billboards across France, actor Woody Harrelson is pictured, arms outstretched in a position recalling that of Jesus Christ on the cross, against a backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad pelvis.

"The plaintiffs stress that the poster represents a naked man, arms outstretched in the exact position of a crucified individual, against a female body in a state of undress," lawyer Jean-Marc Varaut said in a statement.
"This poster deliberately strikes at the conscience of Catholics in using the very symbol of the Christian faith as publicity for a film on pornography," said Varaut.
Varaut is defending ex-cabinet minister Maurice Papon, who will stand trial later this year for deporting Jews during the Second World War.
The controversial film, which won two Academy Award nominations in Los Angeles last week, focuses on the trial of U.S. hard-core pornography publisher Larry Flynt.
According to the plaintiffs -- several dozen Catholic priests and laymen -- the poster's presence in public places is an intolerable attack on religious freedom.
A judge is due to rule on the request on Tuesday.
